sentences.text: This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, being aggrieved by the Award dated 13.05.2019 passed by 12th Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Gwalior (M.P.) (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.848/2017, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement thereof.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, issue of negligence and the liability of the respondents are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, due to death of Neeraj Arya in the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.3,85,000/- along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10858 2 MA-3979-2019 4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the appellants/claimants have preferred the present appeal on the ground that the learned Claims Tribunal has passed the impugned award without proper appreciation of the settled principles of law as well as the facts of the case.

It is contended Smt. Guddi vs Anil Singh Bhadoriya on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45599965/
1 that the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is grossly inadequate and on the lower side.

entities.text: Smt. Guddi vs Anil Singh Bhadoriya
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The deceased was about 16 years of age and was a healthy young boy with a bright future ahead.
However, the learned Claims Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.30,000/- per annum, which is wholly unjustified and does not reflect the prevailing standards.

It is further contended that the learned Claims Tribunal has committed a grave error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation under the conventional heads, such as loss of love and affection,
funeral expenses, and loss of estate.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, it is humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to enhance the compensation and award a just, fair,
and reasonable amount in favour of the claimants, in the interest of justice.
5. On the other hand, learned counsels for the Insurance Company supported the impugned award and prayed for rejection of the appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
On perusal of record of the Claims Tribunal, it is found that the claimants have utterly failed to adduce any substantial evidence in regard to income of the deceased.

Hence, this Court finds it appropriate to assess the income of the deceased as an unskilled person in view of the law laid down in the cases o f Sukhdevi v. Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways,
2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10858 3 MA-3979-2019 3 ACC 134 in which it is held that when documentary proof of income is lacking, income is to be assessed as per the minimum wages applicable.
Therefore, in considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of the income of the deceased as an unskilled person as per Minimum Wages Act in the present case is Rs.7,125/- per month.
8.

sentences.text: As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700, the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects @ 40% has rightly been assessed by Tribunal.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 is to be applied in place of 15 which has been wrongly applied by Claims Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Deceased was bachelor, therefore, he is entitled to get personal expenses i.e. 1/2.
9.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD   Income Rs.7125  Future Prospects@ 40% Rs.1197  After deducting personal expenses 1/2 Rs.5985  Multiplier 18 Rs.1077 Smt. Guddi vs Anil Singh Bhadoriya on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45599965/
2  Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,0  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,0

Total Compensation = Rs.11,87,300/-
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10858  4  10.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.11,87,300/- as against the sum of Rs.3,85,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.8,02,300/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
11. In the result, miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed.
The impugned award i s modified, and the compensation is enhanced by a sum of Rs.8,02,300/-.
The aforesaid enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by Claims Tribunal from the date of deposit of Court fees by the appellants in the present appeal.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12 . In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
13. In view of the foregoing, the miscellaneous appeal stands partly allowed.
